In the memos codebase at /bench/repo, understand how the ListMemos RPC filter expression works:

1. Find the ListMemos RPC and its filter field
   grep -rn 'ListMemos\|list_memos' /bench/repo/proto/ | head -20
   grep -rn 'filter' /bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto 2>/dev/null | head -20

2. Find what parses the filter expression - look for CEL, filter parser, or expression engine
   grep -rn 'filter\|Filter\|parse\|Parse' --include='*.go' /bench/repo/server/service/memo_service.go 2>/dev/null | head -30
   grep -rn 'CEL\|cel\|expr\|filterParser\|ParseFilter' --include='*.go' /bench/repo/server/ | grep -v test | head -30

3. Find the filter/expression engine package
   find /bench/repo -type d -name '*filter*' -o -name '*expr*' -o -name '*cel*' 2>/dev/null | head -10
   grep -rn 'github.com/google/cel\|go.einride.tech/aip\|filter' /bench/repo/go.mod | head -10

4. Find how the filter becomes SQL for each dialect (sqlite, postgres, mysql)
   grep -rn 'filter\|Filter\|where\|WHERE' --include='*.go' /bench/repo/server/store/*memo* 2>/dev/null | grep -v test | head -30
   grep -rn 'ListMemos\|findMemoList' --include='*.go' /bench/repo/server/store/ | grep -v test | head -20

Read the relevant files to understand the complete filter pipeline. Report exact file paths, line numbers, and the parsing engine used.

- codebase-memory: Use the codebase knowledge graph for structural code queries. Triggers on: explore the codebase, understand the architecture, what functions exist, show me the structure, who calls this function, what does X call, trace the call chain, find callers of, show dependencies, impact analysis, dead code, unused functions, high fan-out, refactor candidates, code quality audit, graph query syntax, Cypher query examples, edge types, how to use search_graph.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

## ListMemos Filter Pipeline: Complete Trace

### 1. Proto Definition

**File:** `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, lines 326-339

The `ListMemosRequest` message has a `filter` field (field number 5) documented as:
> "A CEL expression to filter memos."

Available CEL fields: `content`, `creator`, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, `pinned`, `visibility`, `tags`, `has_task_list`, `has_link`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, plus the virtual `now` variable and `duration()` / `timestamp()` functions.

### 2. Service Layer -- Entry Point

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 211-215

When `request.Filter` is non-empty, two things happen:
1. **Validation** (line 212): `s.validateFilter(ctx, request.Filter)` compiles the filter against the current DB dialect to catch syntax errors early. Defined at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go`, lines 336-360.
2. **Accumulation** (line 215): The raw filter string is appended to `memoFind.Filters` (a `[]string`). The service also injects **authorization filters** programmatically -- e.g., `creator_id == %d || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 222) -- so multiple filter strings can be combined.

The `FindMemo.Filters` field is defined at `/bench/repo/store/memo.go`, line 72.

### 3. Parsing Engine -- CEL to IR

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go`

The parsing engine is `github.com/google/cel-go` (v0.28.1, per `go.mod` line 13). The `Engine` struct wraps a `cel.Env` constructed from the schema's `EnvOptions`.

The compilation pipeline (`Engine.Compile`, line 48):
1. `e.env.Compile(filter)` -- CEL parses and type-checks the expression
2. `cel.AstToParsedExpr(ast)` -- converts to the protobuf AST representation (`exprv1.Expr`)
3. `buildCondition(parsed.GetExpr(), ...)` -- walks the CEL AST and builds a **dialect-agnostic IR** (intermediate representation)

The IR is defined in `/bench/repo/internal/filter/ir.go`. Key condition types:
- `LogicalCondition` (AND/OR)
- `NotCondition`
- `ComparisonCondition` (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=)
- `FieldPredicateCondition` (bare boolean field like `pinned`)
- `TextMatchCondition` (contains/startsWith/endsWith on strings)
- `RegexCondition` (field.matches("pattern"))
- `ElementInCondition` ("value" in tags)
- `InCondition` (field in [...])
- `ListComprehensionCondition` (tags.exists/all/exists_one with predicates)
- `ConstantCondition` (constant-folded booleans)

The parser (`/bench/repo/internal/filter/parser.go`) handles:
- Logical operators: `_&&_`, `_||_`, `!_`
- Comparisons: `_==_`, `_!=_`, `_<_`, `_>_`, `_<=_`, `_>=_`
- Membership: `@in`
- Text matching: `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `matches`
- Set operations: `sets.contains`, `sets.intersects`, `sets.equivalent`
- Comprehensions: `exists`, `all`, `exists_one`
- Timestamp accessors: `getFullYear`, `getMonth`, `getDate`, `getDayOfMonth`, `getDayOfWeek`, `getDayOfYear`, `getHours`, `getMinutes`, `getSeconds`
- Constant folding of `now`, `duration("...")`, `timestamp("...")`, and arithmetic

### 4. Schema Definition

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/filter/schema.go`, `NewSchema()` at line 89

Each field has a `Kind` (how it is stored) and per-dialect `Expressions`:
| CEL Field | Kind | Backing Column | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | scalar | `memo.content` | Supports contains/startsWith/endsWith/matches |
| `creator` | scalar | `memo_creator.username` | Wrapped as `'users/' \|\| username`; only == and != |
| `creator_id` | scalar | `memo.creator_id` | Only == and != |
| `created_ts` | scalar | `memo.created_ts` | MySQL wraps with `UNIX_TIMESTAMP()` |
| `updated_ts` | scalar | `memo.updated_ts` | MySQL wraps with `UNIX_TIMESTAMP()` |
| `pinned` | bool_column | `memo.pinned` | Only == and != |
| `visibility` | scalar | `memo.visibility` | Only == and != |
| `tags` | json_list | `memo.payload` -> `$.tags` | Supports comprehensions, set ops, membership |
| `tag` | virtual_alias | alias for `tags` | |
| `has_task_list` | json_bool | `memo.payload` -> `$.property.hasTaskList` | |
| `has_link` | json_bool | `memo.payload` -> `$.property.hasLink` | |
| `has_code` | json_bool | `memo.payload` -> `$.property.hasCode` | |
| `has_incomplete_tasks` | json_bool | `memo.payload` -> `$.property.hasIncompleteTasks` | |

### 5. SQL Rendering -- IR to Dialect-Specific SQL

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/filter/render.go`

The `renderer` converts the IR tree into a `Statement{SQL, Args}` with dialect-specific output for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Key dialect differences:

- **Placeholders:** SQLite/MySQL use `?`; PostgreSQL uses `$1`, `$2`, etc.
- **Column quoting:** SQLite/MySQL use backticks; PostgreSQL uses unquoted `table.column`
- **JSON access:** SQLite/MySQL use `JSON_EXTRACT(col, '$.path')`; PostgreSQL uses `col->'key'` / `col->>'key'`
- **JSON array membership:** SQLite uses `LIKE '%"value"%'`; MySQL uses `JSON_CONTAINS`; PostgreSQL uses `@> jsonb_build_array()`
- **Case-insensitive LIKE:** SQLite uses `memos_unicode_lower()` with explicit `ESCAPE`; PostgreSQL uses `ILIKE`; MySQL relies on collation
- **Regex:** PostgreSQL uses `~`; MySQL/SQLite use `REGEXP`
- **Timestamp accessors:** SQLite uses `strftime`; PostgreSQL uses `EXTRACT(...FROM to_timestamp(col) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')`; MySQL uses native functions like `YEAR()`, `MONTH()`
- **Boolean columns:** SQLite stores as 0/1; PostgreSQL/MySQL use native booleans

### 6. Store Layer -- Final SQL Assembly

**Files:**
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go`, lines 54-63
- `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go`, lines 54-58
- `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go`, lines 65-69

Each driver calls `filter.AppendConditions(ctx, engine, find.Filters, filter.Dialect*, &where, &args)`, which iterates over the `[]string` filters, compiles each one via the engine, and appends the rendered SQL fragments as WHERE clauses. These are combined with other structural WHERE conditions (ID, UID, creator_id, row_status, visibility) using AND.

### Summary: End-to-End Flow

```
HTTP/gRPC request (filter string)
  --> memo_service.go: validateFilter() [compile-only check]
  --> memo_service.go: memoFind.Filters = append(Filters, filter)
  --> store driver (sqlite/postgres/mysql):
      --> filter.DefaultEngine() [singleton, cel.Env from schema]
      --> filter.AppendConditions():
          --> engine.CompileToStatement():
              --> cel-go Compile() [parse + type-check CEL]
              --> cel.AstToParsedExpr() [to protobuf AST]
              --> buildCondition() [AST -> dialect-agnostic IR tree]
              --> renderer.Render() [IR -> SQL + args for target dialect]
          --> append SQL fragment to WHERE clauses
  --> assembled query executed against database
```
